movement_source: row 'Cash earnings', column FY24 (Sep 2024) -> column FY25 (Sep 2025)
headline: NAB's cash earnings decreased by $11 million to $7,091 million in FY25 from $7,102 million in FY24. Statutory net profit was $6,788 million (FY24: $7,063 million). Total operating income increased by $577 million (2.8%) to $20,813 million. Operating performance (income less underlying operating expenses) declined by $188 million due to higher costs and lower credit impairment write-backs, partially offset by higher NII.

drivers.narrative: Increased by $644 million (3.8%). Driven by a $718 million underlying increase from higher average interest earning assets (+$22.5bn, +2.3%) and a 3 bps margin improvement. Partially offset by a $74 million decrease in economic hedges, which was offset in other operating income.

Decreased by $67 million (1.9%). Net fees and commissions fell $132 million due to a $102 million customer remediation charge (vs $35m in FY24) and fee reductions from business disposals ($66m). Trading income rose $33 million, including a $74 million hedge gain offsetting the NII hedge loss. Other income rose $32 million.

Increased by $435 million (4.6%). Underlying expenses rose $305 million driven by salary inflation and technology investment. Notable items included a $130 million payroll review and remediation cost increase. Personnel expenses rose $271 million; Technology $71 million; General $81 million.

The charge increased by $105 million (from $728 million to $833 million), reducing earnings. This reflects a $122 million write-back in FY25 compared to a $205 million write-back in FY24, indicating a deterioration in credit conditions or provisioning.

Tax expense increased by $27 million (0.9%) to $3,002 million. The effective tax rate rose 10 basis points to 29.6%, primarily due to a decrease in the deferred tax asset recognized for U.S. tax losses.

notable_items: Payroll review and remediation costs: $130 million increase in FY25 vs FY24.
limitations: The bridge is built using the bank's stated movements for each component rather than a single consolidated walk chart. All components reconcile exactly to the reported delta of -$11 million.
Capped at 80: credit_impairment_charge -105 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Failed check: drivers_reconcile (drivers +10.0 + residual +0.0 != delta -11.0, tol 1.0)

Capped at 80: nii +644 $m, other_operating_income -67 $m, operating_expenses -435 $m, tax_and_other -27 $m. drivers_reconcile failed, so the parts and the whole disagree. That proves one of these claims is wrong without saying which, so none of them may claim near-certainty.

evidence_records.quote: Group cash earnings reconciliation to statutory net profit

NAB uses cash earnings (rather than statutory net profit attributable to owners of the Company) for its internal management reporting purposes and considers it a better reflection of the Group’s underlying performance.

Cash earnings is not a statutory financial measure and is not presented in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards nor audited or reviewed in accordance with Australian Auditing Standards. Cash earnings is calculated by excluding discontinued operations and certain other items which are included within the statutory net profit attributable to owners of the Company.
